newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VALENCIA AND BARCELONA - STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VALENCIA AND BARCELONA - STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Valencia and Barcelona who meet on Sunday in the Spanish league championship in the Mestalla stadium (1600 gmt).
Strategy: Jorge Valdano's system sees two midfielders play in front of the four-man defence as link-men, with three more pushing up to support a single striker.
The improvised team is likely to have Andoni Zubizarreta in goal with Jorge Otero on the right side of defence, Francisco Ferreira on the left and Ivan Campo and Fernando Caceres the middle.
Vicente Engonga and Xabier Eskurza will be the deep-lying midfielders with veteran Fernando Gomez returning from the bench to play the central distributive role.
Antonio Poyatos will take the right wing, and Claudio Lopez the left, while Brazilian striker Leandro will work as target man.
Strengths: Zubizarreta is the most experienced goalkeeper in Spanish league history and although sometimes prone to embarrassing gaffes, should be especially motivated against his old club.
Winger Claudio Lopez is also unpredictable, but enjoys moments of inspiration which can turn any game, while the elegant Valdano has a superb footballing brain.
The Valencia crowd have had their differences with chairman Paco Roig, but always give the team good backing.

Weaknesses: The players at Valdano's disposal are of a lesser calibre to those at Barcelona and the personnel crisis at the club created by injury, suspension and absence through international duty can only widen further the quality gap.
Valencia will be without a number of key players, most notably Argentine midfielder Ariel Ortega, the man who has revolutionised the team since arriving as a record signing last month.
Other important absences are Goran Vlaovic -- away on international duty with Croatia -- and fellow striker Jose Galvez, who is ill.
Valencia will have all too few match-winners on the field, while Barcelona will be able to leave several on the bench.
Motivation: Every team in Spain likes to beat Barcelona, but Valencia, a city often overshadowed by its larger neighbour on the Mediterranean coast, take a particular pleasure.

Probable team: Goalkeeper-Andoni Zubizarreta defenders-Jorge Otero, Ivan Campo, Fernando Caceres, Francisco Ferreira midfielders-Vicente Engonga, Xabier Eskurza, Antonio Poyatos, Fernando Gomez, Claudio Lopez striker-Leandro.
Strategy: Bobby Robson also plays a 4-5-1, or 4-2-3-1 formation with Ronaldo the lone front man.
